sections.html:
Doña Ana County is in the south of New Mexico along the Texas and Mexico borders. It has more than 219,500 residents and includes the cities of Anthony, Las Cruces and Sunland Park, the Town of Mesilla and the Village of Hatch.

Las Cruces is the county seat and the largest city in southern New Mexico, with 111,385 residents in the 2020 census. It anchors the Mesilla Valley, the farming region on the Rio Grande floodplain.

For a seller, that mix means very different property types under one tax office: city lots in Las Cruces, irrigated farm parcels in the Mesilla Valley and open desert acreage. Tax rates vary with the city, school district and special districts a parcel sits in.

The Doña Ana County Assessor values property. The Doña Ana County Treasurer bills and collects. The Assessor's office does valuation, not taxation.

The state Department of Finance and Administration sets the rate each taxing entity receives, called the mill levy. Cities, school districts and other entities take a share based on their budgets.

The formula is taxable value minus exemptions, multiplied by the mill rate. Taxable value is one-third of assessed value. Check your own district's rate on the Assessor's site.

First-half tax is due November 10 and becomes delinquent after December 10. Second-half tax is due April 10 and becomes delinquent after May 10.

DateEvent
January 1Property valued; liens attach to delinquent real and personal property
January 10Deadline to file claims for refund in District Court
April 10Second half due
May 10Second half delinquent
June 10Delinquent notices mailed and notices of transfer to the state
July 1Treasurer transfers the delinquent roll to the state
October 1Treasurer receives the tax roll from the Assessor
November 1Bills mailed
November 10First half due
December 10First half delinquent

November 10 is the due date, and December 10 is the last day before delinquency charges apply on December 11.

Interest accrues at 1% of the base tax each month until paid, and a 1% penalty accrues for up to five months, with a $5 minimum penalty. A returned check carries a $25 fee.

No law lets a county treasurer waive penalty or interest, and no other body can remove them once accrued. A missing bill is not a defense, because owners must pay on time whether or not a bill arrived.

The consequences escalate over time:

  • Each June the Treasurer mails a notice for any bill 30 or more days delinquent.
  • Delinquent taxes are transferred to the state's Property Tax Division on July 1.
  • Real property with taxes unpaid for two years from the delinquency date can be sold at state public auction.
  • If three or more years of prior taxes are owed, the property is sold unless all years are paid in full by the sale date.
  • Manufactured homes and personal property can be seized and sold after six months.

An owner who cannot pay in full can ask the state Property Tax Division about an installment agreement to stop a sale.

sections.h2: How to protest or reduce your bill
sections.html:
File a valuation protest with the County Assessor within 30 days of the date on the Notice of Value, usually during April. If you miss it, pay the full bill by December 10 and file a claim for refund in District Court by January 10.

A pending protest does not suspend payment. Pay at least the tax on the value not in dispute by December 10, and by May 10 for the second half. If a protest results in a corrected bill, it carries a new delinquency date and arrives at least 30 days before payment is due, without interest or penalty on the amended amount.

New Mexico has no homestead exemption. The relief available is:

  • Head of Family, for a resident whose primary residence it is. You apply once and it continues, one per household.
  • A veteran exemption, which requires a certificate from the state's veteran service commission, taken to the Assessor during the Notice of Value period.
  • A valuation freeze for owners 65 or older or disabled, with modified gross income under $35,000, applied for in three consecutive years before it stays in place while you live there.

Call the Assessor to confirm the current income limit before you apply.

The owner of record on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax, and a tax lien stays on the property regardless of later ownership changes. The Treasurer cites section 7-37-7 NMSA 1978 for this rule.

The county cannot prorate taxes. Any split between buyer and seller is a matter for the sale contract and the closing statement, which a title company prepares. If the property is mortgaged, make sure the lender has paid. The county does not mail an escrowed bill to the owner, though you can request one.

Special situations to watch:

  • A mobile home needs a property tax release from the Assessor before its title can transfer or a moving permit issue, and personal checks are not accepted for the release payment.
  • A land split or combination requires taxes paid in full, including the current year, before the Treasurer issues a Certification of Taxes Paid.
  • A closed business still owes tax for the year if it operated on January 1.

Sellers with farm parcels, inherited land or several years of back tax often choose an as-is cash sale, and the title company pays what is owed from the proceeds.

A practical order of work: get the payoff figure from the Treasurer, confirm your exemptions with the Assessor, then give both numbers to the title company so the closing statement splits the year correctly.

faqs.q: When are Doña Ana County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due November 10 and becomes delinquent after December 10. The second half is due April 10 and becomes delinquent after May 10.

faqs.q: How much are late fees in Doña Ana County?
faqs.a: Interest is 1% of the base tax per month, and a 1% penalty accrues for up to five months, with a $5 minimum. The Treasurer cannot waive either.

faqs.q: Can Doña Ana County property taxes be prorated?
faqs.a: No, the county cannot prorate taxes. Buyers and sellers divide the tax in their contract and at closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest my Doña Ana County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date of the Notice of Value, usually in April. A later claim for refund requires paying the full bill and filing in District Court by January 10.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Doña Ana County property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent taxes move to the state Property Tax Division on July 1. Real property can be sold at state auction when taxes stay unpaid for two years, or sooner when three or more years are owed.
